summary.text: A six-year-old girl with congenital single kidney and chronic kidney disease on peritoneal dialysis presented with fever, a gingival lesion suggestive of linear erythema, gingival pain and difficulty eating and drinking. The initial diagnosis was pneumonia with febrile neutropenia and hypoalbuminemia, and she was admitted to the pediatric ICU, where the marginal and attached gingiva later showed white coloration suggestive of necrosis.

P. aeruginosa was detected in a gingival fragment culture and in blood and nasal secretion cultures, and septic shock was diagnosed. Pathological tooth mobility, bone loss on panoramic radiograph and clinical insertion loss without periodontal pockets were found. Biopsy confirmed inflammatory hyperplastic gingivitis and bone tissue, and the bone tissue culture also grew P. aeruginosa.

Systemic antibiotics (vancomycin, ampicillin-sulbactam, amikacin, piperacillin-tazobactam, polymyxin B, then levofloxacin) were given with supragingival scraping and chlorhexidine, and necrotic gingival mucosa gradually resolved. Bone lesions and mobile deciduous teeth were surgically removed; histopathology showed chronic osteomyelitis and culture was negative. Fifteen days later oral health had improved significantly, and HIV was detected after the six-month treatment period despite earlier negative serology.
